Model workspace and data

Source: vignettes/articles/model_workspace.Rmd
model_workspace.Rmd
library(multimod)

A model’s data can be large. multimod keeps the model structure and the data apart on disk: save_model() writes a workspace, a directory with the R object for the structure and one data file per set, mapping and parameter, in CSV, Arrow IPC or Parquet. load_model() reads it back, with or without the data, and get_data() fetches a table from disk on demand. The generated JuMP and Pyomo code reads the same files at run time, which is why write_jump() and write_pyomo() create a workspace when they are given an empty model_dir.

Layout 

<model_dir>/
  model.rds              the model structure, as saved
  metadata.json          counts and format, for readers outside R
  format.txt             "csv", "ipc" or "parquet"
  sets/<name>/data.*     one file per set, column `member`
  mappings/<name>/data.* one file per mapping, one column per dimension
  parameters/<name>/data.*          dimension columns plus `value`
  parameters/<name>/folded_data/data.*   if the parameter is folded
  variables/<name>/data.*           solution values, after a solve
  solution_log.txt       one line per solution load
  solvers/<backend>/     generated code and the backend's output

Save and load 

toy <- example_models$toy
ws <- tempfile("toy-")
toy <- save_model(toy, ws, format = "csv", verbose = FALSE)
list.files(ws, recursive = TRUE)[1:8]
#> [1] "format.txt"                 "mappings/mappings.csv"     
#> [3] "mappings/mR/data.csv"       "mappings/mTR/data.csv"     
#> [5] "metadata.json"              "model.rds"                 
#> [7] "parameters/parameters.csv"  "parameters/pAvail/data.csv"
toy$base_path == ws
#> [1] TRUE

save_model() returns the model with base_path set to the workspace. With format = "ipc" or "parquet" the data files are Arrow files, smaller and faster to read; both need the ‘arrow’ package, and the generated Julia and Python read them as readily as CSV.

ws_ipc <- tempfile("toy-ipc-")
save_model(toy, ws_ipc, format = "ipc", verbose = FALSE)
list.files(file.path(ws_ipc, "parameters"), recursive = TRUE)
#> [1] "parameters.csv"      "pAvail/data.arrow"   "pCapCost/data.arrow"
#> [4] "pDemand/data.arrow"  "pVarCost/data.arrow"

load_model() reads the structure and, by default, every data table:

m <- load_model(ws, verbose = FALSE)
head(m$parameters$pAvail$data)
#>   tech region value
#> 1 coal  north  0.85
#> 2  gas  north  0.85
#> 3 wind  north  0.90
#> 4 coal  south  0.90
#> 5  gas  south  0.35
#> 6 wind  south  0.25

Data on demand

A large model is loaded without its data and asked for one table at a time. get_data() reads the table from the workspace and caches it in the model object it returns from.

m <- load_model(ws, load_data = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
is.null(m$parameters$pAvail$data)
#> [1] FALSE
get_data(m, "pAvail", type = "parameter")
#>   tech region value
#> 1 coal  north  0.85
#> 2  gas  north  0.85
#> 3 wind  north  0.90
#> 4 coal  south  0.90
#> 5  gas  south  0.35
#> 6 wind  south  0.25
get_data(m, "mTR", type = "mapping")
#>   tech region
#> 1 coal  north
#> 2  gas  north
#> 3 wind  north
#> 4 coal  south
#> 5  gas  south
#> 6 wind  south
get_data(m, "tech", type = "set")
#> [1] "coal" "gas"  "wind"

Changing data

update_parameter() replaces a parameter’s table; with auto_save = TRUE the file in the workspace is rewritten at the same time.

d <- get_data(m, "pDemand", type = "parameter")
d$value <- d$value * 1.1
m <- update_parameter(m, "pDemand", d, auto_save = TRUE)
read.csv(file.path(ws, "parameters", "pDemand", "data.csv"))
#>   region value
#> 1  north  1100
#> 2  south   660

The structure is unchanged, so the model can be re-solved on the new data through any route, for example in R:

m <- load_model(ws, verbose = FALSE)
solve_highs(m, attach = FALSE)$objective
#> [1] 217800

Solutions

The file routes write their results under solvers/<backend>/solution/. With load_results = TRUE (the default when a model is passed), solve_gmpl(), solve_jump() and solve_pyomo() read the variable values into model$variables[[name]]$solution, copy them to variables/, and append a line to solution_log.txt, so the workspace always holds the latest solution and a record of when it was loaded.

r <- solve_jump(m, ws)
r$model$variables$vGen$solution
r$model$solution_metadata$variables_loaded
readLines(file.path(ws, "solution_log.txt"))

Folded data

A folded parameter (see vignette("folding")) keeps both tables: the original under data.* and the reduced one under folded_data/data.*. save_model() writes both, load_model() reads both, and the writers take the folded table when the model is folded.

Reading the files elsewhere

The data files are plain CSV or Arrow and need nothing from multimod:

import pyarrow.feather as feather
demand = feather.read_feather("ws/parameters/pDemand/data.arrow")
using Arrow, DataFrames
demand = DataFrame(Arrow.Table("ws/parameters/pDemand/data.arrow"))

metadata.json lists the counts and the format so a reader can orient itself without R.

cat(readLines(file.path(ws, "metadata.json")), sep = "\n")
#> {
#>   "name": "toy",
#>   "desc": "two-region capacity expansion toy model",
#>   "saved": "2026-10-19 22:17:56",
#>   "format": "csv",
#>   "compression": null,
#>   "compression_level": null,
#>   "n_sets": 2,
#>   "n_parameters": 4,
#>   "n_mappings": 2,
#>   "n_equations": 3,
#>   "n_variables": 3
#> }
